# Differential analysis: Contrast-based approach

## Load data

We use the full dataset for this analysis

```{r}
se <- readRDS("./datasets/whole_vHC_dataset.rds")
dge <- DGEList(assay(se, "counts"))
mm <- model.matrix(~ 0 + group, data=as.data.frame(colData(se)))
dge <- calcNormFactors(dge)
# Filter lowly expressed genes
keep <- filterByExpr(dge, mm, min.count = 10)
se <- se[keep, ]

# First we use SVA correction to capture latent technical variation
# There are two embedded methods to estimate the number of SVs: BE and LEEK
# We take a look at both of their estimation
set.seed(1)
tmp <- SEtools::svacor(se, ~ 0 + group, numSVmethod = "be", method = "vst")
tmp <- SEtools::svacor(se, ~ 0 + group, numSVmethod = "leek", method = "vst")
# we use 6 SVs as "BE" suggested
se <- SEtools::svacor(se, ~ 0 + group, n.sv = 6, method = "vst")
se <- log2FC(se, "corrected", controls = grep("Ctrl", se$group), isLog = TRUE)  # calculate logFC relative to the mean of control samples
```

## DEA 

```{r}
dge <- calcNormFactors(DGEList(assay(se)))
formula <- as.formula(paste(c("~ 0 + group", grep("^SV[0-9]+$",colnames(colData(se)),value = TRUE)), collapse = "+"))
mm <- model.matrix(formula , data = as.data.frame(colData(se))) # include SVs in the model matrix
dge <- estimateDisp(dge, mm)
fit <- glmQLFit(dge, mm, pseudocount = 0.5)

# Define the constrasts to test for
# Here in the contrast-based approach, we can define contrasts explicityly rather than relying on model coefficients
# This avoids the reference sex bias described in the pitfalls section
contrast <- makeContrasts(
  Stress_vs_CTRL = (groupFemale_Stress + groupMale_Stress) / 2 - (groupFemale_Ctrl + groupMale_Ctrl) / 2,  # Overall stress effect, averaged equally across both sexes
  F_M_Stress = (groupFemale_Stress - groupFemale_Ctrl) - (groupMale_Stress - groupMale_Ctrl),  # Sex*Stress interaction: does the stress response differ between sexes?
  F_vs_M_Ctrl = groupFemale_Ctrl - groupMale_Ctrl,  # Baseline sex difference (in Ctrls only) 
  F_vs_M_Stress = groupFemale_Stress - groupMale_Stress,  # Sex difference in Stress group
  F_Stress = groupFemale_Stress - groupFemale_Ctrl, # Stress response in females
  M_Stress = groupMale_Stress - groupMale_Ctrl, # Stress response in males
  levels = mm)

Results_stress <- addlogFCSE(as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast[, "Stress_vs_CTRL"]),Inf)))
# Difference stress vs no stress

Results_M <- addlogFCSE(as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast[, "M_Stress"]),Inf))) 
# Difference stress vs no stress in males

Results_F <- addlogFCSE(as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast[, "F_Stress"]),Inf))) 
# Difference stress vs no stress in females

Results_sex <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast[, "F_vs_M_Ctrl"]),Inf)) 
# Difference male vs female in Ctrl samples

Results_interaction <- addlogFCSE(as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast[,"F_M_Stress"]),Inf)))
# Difference in response to stress between sexes

Results <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast),Inf)) 
# All results

# save all the DEA results in SE object
rowData(se)$DEA.Stress_vs_CTRL <- addlogFCSE(as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast[, "Stress_vs_CTRL"]),Inf)))
rowData(se)$DEA.M_Stress <- addlogFCSE(as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast[, "M_Stress"]),Inf)))
rowData(se)$DEA.F_Stress <- addlogFCSE(as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast[, "F_Stress"]),Inf)))
rowData(se)$DEA.F_vs_M_Ctrl <- addlogFCSE(as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast[, "F_vs_M_Ctrl"]),Inf)))
rowData(se)$DEA.F_vs_M_Stress <- addlogFCSE(as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast[, "F_vs_M_Stress"]),Inf)))
rowData(se)$DEA.interaction <- addlogFCSE(as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast[,"F_M_Stress"]),Inf)))
rowData(se)$DEA.overall_result <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast),Inf))

# use stageR (two-stage FDR correction) to correct the Pvalue for interaction
# Here we first try to use the pvalue from All Results as the input of screening
pScreen <- Results$PValue
names(pScreen) <- rownames(Results)
pConfirmation <- cbind(Interaction = Results_interaction[row.names(Results),"PValue"])
stageRObj <- stageR(pScreen = pScreen, pConfirmation = pConfirmation, pScreenAdjusted = FALSE)
stageRObj <- stageWiseAdjustment(object = stageRObj, method = "none", alpha = 0.05)
adj_PVals <- getAdjustedPValues(stageRObj, onlySignificantGenes = FALSE, order = FALSE) #returns NA for non-significant gene in pScreen
adj_PVals <- as.data.frame(adj_PVals)
Results_interaction$staged.FDR <- adj_PVals[rownames(Results_interaction),]$"Interaction"

M_signif <- rownames(Results_M[Results_M$FDR < 0.05, ])
F_signif <- rownames(Results_F[Results_F$FDR < 0.05, ])
intDEGs <- rownames(na.omit(Results_interaction[Results_interaction$staged.FDR < 0.05, ]))
intDEGs
```

### Fig 6C

Correlation between interaction logFC and baseline logFC between sexes

```{r}
Results_interaction$logFC.Sex <- Results_sex[row.names(Results_interaction), "logFC"]
Results_interaction$logFC.stressMales <- Results_M[row.names(Results_interaction), "logFC"] 

Results_interaction2 <- Results_interaction[which(Results_interaction$staged.FDR < 0.15 & abs(Results_interaction$logFC) > 0.1),]
ct <- cor.test(Results_interaction2$logFC, Results_interaction2$logFC.Sex)
fig6c <- ggplot(Results_interaction2, aes(logFC.Sex, logFC)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "darkgray") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "darkgray") + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(formula = y ~ 0 + x, method = "lm") + 
  theme_bw() +

  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = -Inf, label = paste0(" R=", round(ct$estimate,2)," ***\n"), hjust = 0, vjust = 0)
fig6c
```

## Improved stageR Strategy

When we use the `All Results` to do FDR correction, there are a lot of genes that are driven by baseline sex difference but the stress effect of them are not obvious. So in the next chunk, we only use stress-relevan contrasts in screening, so that the screening is more targeted increases power

```{r}
Results2 <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast[, c("F_Stress", "M_Stress", "F_M_Stress", "Stress_vs_CTRL")]),Inf))
pScreen2 <- Results2$PValue
names(pScreen2) <- rownames(Results2)

pConfirmation2 <- cbind(Interaction = Results_interaction[row.names(Results2),"PValue"])

stageRObj2 <- stageR(pScreen = pScreen2, pConfirmation = pConfirmation2, pScreenAdjusted = FALSE)
stageRObj2 <- stageWiseAdjustment(object = stageRObj2, method = "none", alpha = 0.05)

adj_PVals2 <- getAdjustedPValues(stageRObj2, onlySignificantGenes = FALSE, order = FALSE) #returns NA for non-significant gene in pScreen
adj_PVals2 <- as.data.frame(adj_PVals2)

Results_interaction$staged.FDR <- adj_PVals2[rownames(Results_interaction),]$"Interaction"
intDEGs2 <- rownames(na.omit(Results_interaction[Results_interaction$staged.FDR < 0.05, ]))
intDEGs2
write.table(intDEGs2, "./objects/interaction_genes_swim_full_dataset.txt")  # for later use 
write.table(Results_interaction, "./objects/DEA_interaction_result_swim_full_dataset.txt")  # for later use
rowData(se)$DEA.subset_overall_result <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, contrast = contrast[, c("F_Stress", "M_Stress", "F_M_Stress", "Stress_vs_CTRL")]),Inf))
# save the staged.FDR in SE for interaction for later use
rowData(se)$Interaction_staged.FDR <- adj_PVals2[rownames(se),]$"Interaction"
```

### Fig 6I 

In next chunk we ask: does female stress response differ systematically from male response? To answer this, we fit a regression of (female logFC - male logFC) ~ male logFC. We did this in three different gene sets: DEGs from full dataset; balanced DEGs; DEGs from balanced data.

```{r}
# Gene set 1. DEGs from differential analysis of the full dataset, both sexes pooled
merge_M_F <- merge(Results_M, Results_F, by = "row.names", suffix = c(".males",".females"))
m1 <- merge_M_F[which(merge_M_F$Row.names %in% row.names(Results_stress)[which(Results_stress$FDR < 0.05)]),]
# Here this gene set is selected form the analysis which is dominated by males (more samples in the data). 
# So we might have detected more DEGs in males (since we have more power there), which could have led to a bias towards males
# # Thus we also use two other different gene sets.

# Gene set 2. balanced DEGs. 
# Take the same number of top male DEGs as female DEGs, to avoid male-dominated gene selection
balanced_degs <- union(head(row.names(Results_M), sum(Results_F$FDR < 0.05)), row.names(Results_F)[which(Results_F$FDR < 0.05)])  # Since female has less significant genes than male, we extract the number of female DEGs
m2 <- merge_M_F[which(merge_M_F$Row.names %in% balanced_degs),]

# Gene set 3. DEGs from a sex-balanced dataset
# Here we select equal number of males and females, then re-run the differential analysis
# This also removes the power imbalance between sexes
# To avoid an odd sampling, we do multiple permutations for this, and average the results for final outcome
n_perm <- 100
library(BiocParallel)
register(MulticoreParam(workers = 10))
set.seed(1234)
slopes_balanced_data <- bplapply(1:n_perm, function(i){
  # cat("Round: ", i, "/", n_perm, "\n")

  # resample males each iteration
  # In our data, females only exist in two batches: Privitera.E2 and vonZiegler.E3
  # To balance also between different batches, we select 2 ctrl males and 3 stress males from Privitera.E1 batch (the reason to select from this batch is that in MDS plot, this batch is the closest one from batch vonZiegler.E3)
  batch_with_both_sexes <- colnames(se)[se$Experiment %in% c("vonZiegler.E3", "Privitera.E2")]
  male_ctrl_Privitera.E1 <- sample(colnames(se)[se$Experiment == "Privitera.E1" & se$group == "Male_Ctrl"], 2, replace = FALSE)
  male_stress_Privitera.E1 <- sample(colnames(se)[se$Experiment == "Privitera.E1" & se$group == "Male_Stress"], 3, replace = FALSE)
  se_sub <- se[,c(batch_with_both_sexes, male_ctrl_Privitera.E1, male_stress_Privitera.E1)]
  # In the end we have 56 samples (14 in each group)

  # filter
  mm <- model.matrix(~ 0 + group, data = as.data.frame(colData(se_sub)))
  dge <- calcNormFactors(DGEList(assay(se_sub)))
  se_sub <- se_sub[filterByExpr(dge, mm, min.count = 10), ]

  # SVA correction
  suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(invisible(capture.output(
    se_sub <- SEtools::svacor(se_sub, ~ 0 + group, n.sv = 2, method = "vst")
  ))))
  
  # DEA
  formula <- as.formula(paste(c("~ 0 + group", grep("^SV[0-9]+$", colnames(colData(se_sub)), value = TRUE)), collapse = "+"))
  mm <- model.matrix(formula, data = as.data.frame(colData(se_sub)))
  dge <- calcNormFactors(DGEList(assay(se_sub)))
  dge <- estimateDisp(dge, mm)
  fit_perm <- glmQLFit(dge, mm, prior.count = 0.5)
  contrast <- makeContrasts(
    Stress_vs_CTRL = (groupFemale_Stress + groupMale_Stress)/2 - (groupFemale_Ctrl + groupMale_Ctrl)/2,
    F_M_Stress     = (groupFemale_Stress - groupFemale_Ctrl) - (groupMale_Stress - groupMale_Ctrl),
    F_vs_M_Ctrl    = groupFemale_Ctrl - groupMale_Ctrl,
    F_vs_M_Stress    = groupFemale_Stress - groupMale_Stress,
    F_Stress       = groupFemale_Stress - groupFemale_Ctrl,
    M_Stress       = groupMale_Stress - groupMale_Ctrl,
    levels = mm)
  Results_stress <- as.data.frame(topTags(glmQLFTest(fit_perm, contrast = contrast[, "Stress_vs_CTRL"]), Inf))
  m_perm <- merge_M_F[merge_M_F$Row.names %in% rownames(Results_stress)[Results_stress$FDR < 0.05], ]

  if (nrow(m_perm) < 5) {
    return(NA) 
    cat("Too few DEGs!")}  # skip if too few DEGs
  
  # return regression table
  coef(summary(lm(logFC.females - logFC.males ~ 0 + logFC.males, data = m_perm)))[,-3]
})

# Summarize
slopes_balanced_data <- as.data.frame(slopes_balanced_data)  # in this table, each column is one permutation
colnames(slopes_balanced_data) <- paste0("balancedData_permutation", seq(1:n_perm))
cat("Median slope:", median(as.numeric(slopes_balanced_data["Estimate",])), "\n")
cat("Mean slope:", mean(as.numeric(slopes_balanced_data["Estimate",])), "\n")
cat("All p-values significant:", all(as.numeric(slopes_balanced_data["Pr(>|t|)",]) < 0.05), "\n")
# For 100 permutations, p-values are all significant
```

```{r}
# ======== Slope analysis across all three gene sets ========
# Model: (female logFC - male logFC) ~ male logFC
# If the slope is significantly non-zero, it means genes with a stronger male stress response also tend to show a bigger male vs. female difference 
# i.e. the sex difference isn't random noise, it scales with the strength of the response itself. 
# If the slope were ~0 and non-significant, it would suggest no such relationship
stats <- as.data.frame(t(sapply(list(full = m1, balancedDEGs = m2), \(x){
  coef(summary(lm(logFC.females - logFC.males ~ 0 + logFC.males, data = x)))[,-3]  # drop the t-statistic
  })))
anno_stat <- paste0(" ", row.names(stats), ": slope=", round(stats[,1], 3), "; p=", round(stats[,3], 4))
anno_stat <- c(
  anno_stat,
  paste0(" balancedData(", n_perm, " permutations):\nmedian slope=", 
         sprintf("%.3f", median(as.numeric(slopes_balanced_data["Estimate",]))), 
         "; all p<0.05")
)

fig6i <- ggplot(m1, aes(logFC.males, logFC.females)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "darkgray") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "darkgray") + 
  theme_bw() + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2.5, 2.5), ylim = c(-1.5, 2.5)) + 
  geom_abline(slope = 1) + geom_point(alpha = 0.1, size = 0.3) + 
  geom_smooth(formula = y ~ 0 + x, method = "lm") +
  labs(x = "logFC upon Stress in males", y = "logFC upon Stress in females") +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(size = 10)) + 
  annotate("text", label = paste0("\n", paste(anno_stat, collapse = "\n")), x = 2.7, y = -Inf, hjust = 1, vjust = -0.25, size = 2.5)
fig6i
```

In the plot we see the slope is slighly negative (the regression slope falls below y=x curve), in all results from the three gene sets. This indicates that females show slightly weaker stress response in our experiments.

# Supplement Figure 3: Check Poorness-of-fit

To test whether our genes violated the assumption of the negative binomial model

```{r}
pval_poorlyfit <- edgeR::gof(fit)$gof.pvalues
names(pval_poorlyfit) <- rownames(fit$coefficients)
rowData(se)$poorlyfit.pvalue <- pval_poorlyfit[rownames(se)]

all_genes <- rownames(fit$coefficients)
stress_genes <- rownames(Results_stress[Results_stress$FDR < 0.05, ])

df_combined <- rbind(
  data.frame(neg_log10p = -log10(rowData(se)$poorlyfit.pvalue), group = "All genes", gene = gsub(".+\\.", "", names(rowData(se)$poorlyfit.pvalue))),
  data.frame(neg_log10p = -log10(rowData(se[stress_genes,])$poorlyfit.pvalue), group = "Stress DEGs", gene = gsub(".+\\.", "", names(rowData(se[stress_genes,])$poorlyfit.pvalue))),
  data.frame(neg_log10p = -log10(rowData(se[intDEGs2,])$poorlyfit.pvalue), group = "Interaction DEGs", gene = gsub(".+\\.", "", names(rowData(se[intDEGs2,])$poorlyfit.pvalue)))
)
df_combined$group <- factor(df_combined$group, levels = c("All genes", "Stress DEGs", "Interaction DEGs"))

# define outliers
outliers <- subset(
  df_combined,
  group == "Interaction DEGs" & neg_log10p > 50 & is.finite(neg_log10p)  # choose your threshold
)

# Wilcoxon test 
w1 <- wilcox.test(rowData(se)$poorlyfit.pvalue[stress_genes], rowData(se)$poorlyfit.pvalue)  # Stress DEGs vs. All genes
w2 <- wilcox.test(rowData(se)$poorlyfit.pvalue[intDEGs2],    rowData(se)$poorlyfit.pvalue[stress_genes])  # Interaction DEGs vs. Stress DEGs
res_wilcox <- data.frame(
  comparison = c("Stress DEGs vs. All genes", "Interaction DEGs vs. Stress DEGs"),
  n1 = c(length(stress_genes), length(intDEGs2)),
  n2 = c(length(all_genes), length(stress_genes)),
  median_neglog10p_1 = c(median(-log10(rowData(se)$poorlyfit.pvalue[stress_genes])), median(-log10(rowData(se)$poorlyfit.pvalue[intDEGs2]))),
  median_neglog10p_2 = c(median(-log10(rowData(se)$poorlyfit.pvalue)), median(-log10(rowData(se)$poorlyfit.pvalue[stress_genes]))),
  p = c(w1$p.value, w2$p.value)
)
res_wilcox

# violin plot
y_top <- max(df_combined$neg_log10p[is.finite(df_combined$neg_log10p)])
fmt   <- function(p) paste0("p = ", format.pval(p, digits = 2))

pof <- ggplot(df_combined, aes(x = group, y = neg_log10p, fill = group)) +
  geom_violin(scale = "width", bounds = c(0, 50)) + # estimate the kernel density using data points with y<50
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1, outlier.size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = outliers,
    aes(label = gene),
    size = 3,
    max.overlaps = Inf
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "-log10(p)", 
       title = "Poorness of NB model fit") + 
  ggsignif::geom_signif(
  comparisons = list(c("All genes", "Stress DEGs"),
                     c("Stress DEGs", "Interaction DEGs")),
  annotations = paste0("p = ", format.pval(res_wilcox$p, digits = 2)),
  y_position = y_top * c(1.01, 1.05),
  tip_length = 0, textsize = 3.5, color = "grey50"
)
pof
ggsave("./supplements/supp_pof.pdf", plot = pof)
```
